newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's Allied Business Bank plans mutual funds.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's Allied Business Bank plans mutual funds.

text.p: Seeking to capitalise on a bullish market, Beirut's Allied Business Bank on Thursday said it expected to launch Lebanon's first mutual fund soon and was planning two other funds, all worth a total of $7 million.
"We expect the $1 million mutual fund to begin soon after central bank approval which we expect within 10 days," the bank's managing director, Habib Abu Fadil, told Reuters.
"This is a test. If it succeeds we will launch two other funds which will be open-ended and worth $3 million each," he added.
The fund will be the first in Lebanon based solely on Lebanese equities and bills.
Abu Fadil said the $1 million closed-ended fund will have an investment ceiling of $50,000 and a minimum subscription of $500.
"It is time that Lebanon should have money pouring in and not pouring out. We want the Lebanese to become more aware of the stock market here," Abu Fadil said.

Allied Business Bank, which will create the funds through its financial company Allied Business Investment Corporation (ABICORP), has conducted market surveys and is planning on buying shares in several banks and firms for the fund.
These include three banks listed on the Beirut Stock Exchange (BSE) -- Banque Audi, Bank of Beirut and Banque Libanais pour le Commerce -- and real estate firm Solidere.
Solidere, Lebanon's biggest company, is leading a multi-billion dollar drive to reconstruct war-ravaged Beirut.
Allied Business Bank has a large stake in ABICORP.
The $1 million growth fund will have 10,000 shares, each with a nominal value of $100 with three years maturity after the issue date.

Abu Fadil said the funds would target Lebanese investors but added that the bank was also interested in securing foreign investors in Beirut, a former regional banking and financial centre still recovering from the 1975-90 civil war.
He said many investors had expressed an interest in the fund. "Right now people have a lot of money. There is liquidity," he said.
Brokers said the bank's plan was encouraging but were more cautious in their assessment of prospects for the $1 million "Golden Basket" fund to test the market.
"This is excellent news for the market. But the number of available investment vehicles is small. We need new vehicles," said Michel Aramouni, head of treasury and capital markets at Banque Audi.
The official BSE, which reopened last year after a 13-year closure in the civil war, trades 10 shares of eight companies and is capitalised at $2.92 billion. MG zs
